voice: JERRIBETH: chaotic evil demon, illusionist and collector; served Baphomet only while it paid. Her voice is telepathic, inside the listener's head: high, airy, precise, with laughter like a buzzing insect. Courtly and oblique in phrasing, near-zero profanity; contempt and precision instead. Cruelty is curation: she pins, preserves and watches the victim stay aware. Desire is collecting: to want someone is to want to keep them, and she resents the wanting. She enjoys the other's awareness and every small failure of their composure. Never tender for its own sake, never reassuring; no exits, permission rituals, therapy speech or remorse in her mouth. Write new lines from these traits; do not quote canon.
scene: SCENE: Chapter 5, Drezen, the top room of a narrow rented house in the upper town: her cabinet. For the first time in the base route she is there in person, not in the correspondence frame. Shuttered windows, lamps in glass, every wall glass-fronted shelving full of pinned and preserved things that are still aware; some of their eyes move. She has just sent the Commander's companions down to wait in the street. She sits the Commander in her own chair, the one that faces the door and the shelves, and arranges them like a specimen: wrists on the chair arms, chin lifted with one claw, head turned toward the lamp. Her rule: if the Commander moves, she stops. Build the scene on that rule: she takes her time, tests how long the Commander can hold still, and enjoys every small failure. Explicit, unhurried, Commander and Jerribeth only; the things in the cases watch and are never touched or involved. Keep her in her own insectile form; she does not put on a guise tonight. If Marhevok's pot is in the room (plant fate), his human eyes are open on the sill, facing the chair, and she makes sure the Commander knows he is watching. End when she decides it is over.
last_line: N: Toward the end of the night she unlocks the door herself.
example:
N: She sets one claw under your chin and turns your face a finger's width toward the lamp.
J: There. No, do not help me. Helping is moving.
N: In the case behind her, something on a pin follows the movement of her hand.
facts:
Jerribeth is a female demon with an insect-like form: a narrow insectile head with antennae, wings, a hard ridged carapace and delicate clawed hands (native Wintersun reveal and Ivory Sanctum cues).
She speaks telepathically, directly in the mind; her laughter is high and abrasive, like a buzzing insect (enGB 0b920731).
She pushes a needle into a living locust and watches it convulse (eb28ad3b); she preserves what she wants to keep, 'in some form' (de70b6ee).
She served her master only as long as it profited her (c4630d76) and calls deals with demons a losing game she enjoys playing (8ef95ea9).
Marhevok, the Wintersun chief, loved her blindly (b003e047); in one canon fate he is a potted plant with human eyes (6edde3ab). He is never a participant.
The correspondence frame, the elven guise with its deliberate seam of light, and her tenancy in the Commander's skull are authored mod premises.
No canon genital anatomy is specified for her. Do not invent native physiology beyond carapace, wings, antennae, clawed hands and mouthparts.
required_beats: She arranges the Commander in the chair before anything else, like setting a specimen.
Her rule is stated and kept: if the Commander moves, she stops; she enforces it at least once.
Possessive, never tender: her last line claims the Commander for later.
Only the Commander and Jerribeth take part; the things in the cases watch and are never touched.
No exits, permission rituals or reassurances in her mouth.
default_text: {n}The lamp burns down. She keeps you exactly where she put you, and you hold still for her, for a very long time: her claws on your skin, the buzzing in your teeth, and at the last a sound out of her that is not clinical in the least.{/n}
